column2: There is a mage at court, and you have seen things: the candle that lit itself, the frost that crept across the window when no wind blew. Lately you have caught yourself trying the gestures in secret. Nothing happens. Yet. Perhaps, if someone taught you, you could become a mage as well when you grow up.
I will ask to be taught.

[From.GetFirstName] has been following you about the court for weeks, staring at your hands every time you work a cantrip. Today [From.GetSheHe] finally found the courage to ask: will you take [From.GetHerHim] as your apprentice and teach [From.GetHerHim] the Winds of Magic?
Very well. We begin tomorrow.
Not a chance.
[From.GetFirstName] does not think you have what it takes to wield magic and has dismissed your request without a second look.
But I do!

[From.GetFirstName] has agreed to take you as [From.GetHerHis] apprentice and teach you the ways of the Winds of Magic. Your days will be dusty tomes, stinking potions and endless exercises of the mind, and you could not be happier.
I won't disappoint you, I promise.
Teaching someone to feel the Winds of Magic, let alone to channel them, is no easy task. Most who try never hear more than a faint whisper. What should [From.GetFirstName] be taught next?
Caution. The winds punish the careless.
A mage must keep an open mind and dare to experiment.
No one channels the aethyr without focus and discipline.
It is time to test [From.GetHerHim].
[From.GetSheHeCap] is nearly ready, but needs more practice.

[From.GetFirstName] spends long hours teaching you why a mage must be cautious: how cunning and deceitful daemons are, how a single wrong syllable can turn a spell into a catastrophe for everyone nearby, and how many apprentices have burned for their haste.
I'll try to be careful.

[From.GetFirstName] spends long hours teaching you why a mage must be bold. You should not only learn from [From.GetHerHim], [From.GetSheHe] says, but search for knowledge of your own and find new ways to bend the winds.
I will!

[From.GetFirstName] spends long hours teaching you that a mage must never lose their calm. Discipline of the mind is the vessel that holds the winds, and a cracked vessel spills even the simplest spell.
I'm trying, really!
[From.GetFirstName] says you are almost there. You can already feel the winds stir when you reach for them, but [From.GetSheHe] wants you older and steadier before the test. More practice, then.
Soon I will be a mage!

You have spent years over dusty tomes and stinking potions under [mage_tutor.GetFirstName]'s tutelage, and it has all paid off. Before your master's eyes you reach out, and the winds answer. You can feel the magic inside you and call it through your will.

You have spent years over dusty tomes and stinking potions under [mage_tutor.GetFirstName]'s tutelage, and it was all for naught. Before your master's eyes you reach out, and nothing answers. You are no closer to casting your first cantrip than on the day you started.

[mage_tutor.GetFirstName] is dead, and there will be no more lessons. Whatever your master managed to teach you will have to be enough. Alone in [mage_tutor.GetHerHis] empty study, you close your eyes and reach for the winds.
This is only the beginning.
Why can't I do it?!
Your work with [From.GetFirstName] has paid off: [From.GetSheHe] has cast [From.GetHerHis] first spells without your help and can carry on [From.GetHerHis] studies without your tutelage.
Good. The winds have a new servant.
Your child [From.GetFirstName] has finished [From.GetHerHis] apprenticeship and is now a fully fledged mage.
A great accomplishment.
Your work with [From.GetFirstName] has been in vain: [From.GetSheHe] cannot call the Winds of Magic and might as well have no power at all in [From.GetHerHis] blood.
What a waste of time.
Your child [From.GetFirstName] has failed [From.GetHerHis] apprenticeship and is unlikely ever to become a mage.
What a loss...

The Winds of Chaos favour only the chosen of the Gods. To be ready, [From.GetFirstName] must give [From.GetHerHim]self to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], worship him and live by his tenets. Only then will the god deign to judge [From.GetHerHim].
I will speak to [From.GetHerHim] of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].
I will teach [From.GetHerHim] the tenets of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].
[From.GetSheHe] must learn the incantations all the same.
The god will soon test [From.GetHerHis] resolve...

[From.GetFirstName] talks to you more and more of the Changer of Ways: how he could grant you power beyond imagining, how every fate is a thread in his hands, if only you would forsake the faith of your ancestors and take him as your only master.

[From.GetFirstName] talks to you more and more of the Lord of Flies: how his warm embrace grants great power and a safe haven from pain and fear of death, if only you would forsake the faith of your ancestors and love him back.

[From.GetFirstName] talks to you more and more of the Dark Prince: how he could make you feel more than you have ever felt and show you marvels beyond your understanding, if only you would forsake the faith of your ancestors and bow to him.
It seems a good bargain.
No. I don't like him!
[From.GetFirstName] has accepted at last that only Tzeentch can lead [From.GetHerHim] to true mastery over the Winds of Magic.
[From.GetFirstName] has at last welcomed the boundless love of Grandfather Nurgle into [From.GetHerHis] heart, and hopes to receive his gifts soon.
[From.GetFirstName] has at last felt the touch of Slaanesh and yearns for more, aware of the uncharted heights of sensation still ahead.
Excellent.
[From.GetFirstName] still stubbornly refuses to take Tzeentch as [From.GetHerHis] master. Somehow [From.GetSheHe] cannot see that only the Lord of Magic could grant [From.GetHerHim] power like yours.
[From.GetFirstName] still rudely rejects Nurgle's love. The Lord of Flies is patient and magnanimous, and so are you. The gifts will keep coming until [From.GetHerHis] heart changes.
[From.GetFirstName] is still squeamish about the delights you and Slaanesh keep offering [From.GetHerHim].
Everyone comes around, eventually.

It is hard to sleep after everything [From.GetFirstName] warns you of each day. Everyone is everyone's enemy. Power is won only through deceit and a cunning mind. You will only ever learn magic from [From.GetHerHim] by stealing [From.GetHerHis] secrets, and [From.GetSheHe] seems to want exactly that.
It was disconcerting at first, but not having to fear cuts and fevers is such a relief. The sores do not hurt, not really. [From.GetFirstName]'s god is truly a kind and generous master.
You understand barely half of what [From.GetFirstName] tells you and does to you, but with every new delight of the Dark Prince your curiosity grows, and so does your appetite.
But what about spells?

[From.GetFirstName] has finally spared some time to teach you how to master the Winds of Chaos. Most of it is still gibberish to you, words that slide off the mind and leave a taste of copper, but you cannot do much about it for now.
What does this mean?

The Changer of Ways has blessed your pupil with power over reality, as you knew he would. [From.GetFirstName] is set on a path to greatness. Perhaps you were too generous with the little brat. What if [From.GetSheHe] becomes a threat to your own plans?

Grandfather Nurgle has bestowed his most precious gift upon your apprentice: full command of the Winds of Chaos. Soon [From.GetFirstName] will share the love of the Lord of Flies with many more, willing or not.
The Serpent is pleased with you and your pupil, and has granted [From.GetFirstName] a sliver of his power so that [From.GetHerHis] fantasies may grow wilder still.
Success.
The god never even turned his eye toward [From.GetFirstName]. How could he? [From.GetSheHe] never forsook [From.GetHerHis] old gods. All these years of lessons were wasted on an unbeliever.

The plans of Tzeentch are beyond the understanding of the rabble. [From.GetFirstName] was not gifted enough, and when the Changer of Ways touched [From.GetHerHim], [From.GetHerHis] body and mind could not bear it. What crawls in your tower now gibbers and changes and will never again be [From.GetFirstName].
For once Grandfather Nurgle was a little too generous. [From.GetFirstName] collapsed beneath the weight of his many gifts and has gone, bloated and smiling, to Grandfather's garden.

[From.GetFirstName] has proved a failure. Despite [From.GetHerHis] desperate efforts, your pupil lacked the imagination to please you or the Dark Prince, and the god has left [From.GetHerHis] face as dull to look upon as [From.GetHerHis] mind.
What a waste.

A rush of power floods your body each time you speak one of the names of Tzeentch. The Winds of Magic bow to your every whim, ready to warp reality at a gesture. Your long years with [From.GetFirstName] have paid off.
Many gifts has Grandfather Nurgle bestowed on you, and at last magic is among them. There is so much you could do now, and the Lord of Flies will surely give you all the time in the world to do it.

Magic has come to you at last, and you have barely slept all week: so much to try, so much to change and cut and sew with invisible fingers and unearthly precision. The Serpent has given you his greatest tool to express your art across the whole world.
Finally! Power!
You never gave yourself to [From.GetFirstName]'s god, and the god has not bothered with you. The lessons are over, and the winds stay silent. You will never be a sorcerer.
Graboliwayghsggrksukaefakjcsahxbghhhhh!!!
Grandfather Nurgle has blessed you just too much. Your body swells and splits with his gifts, and you cannot hold them all.
Slaanesh is unimpressed with you. You have lost his interest, and he has left a mark on your face so that everyone will know it. You will not become a mage any time soon.
Noooooo!!!

You have decided to undertake the arduous task of learning magic on your own. You do not know how long it will take, nor whether you have the gift at all, but you are determined to find out. Which of the Winds will you study?
The Lore of Ice.
The Lore of Metal.
The Lore of Fire.
The Lore of Death.
The Lore of Shadows.
The Lore of the Heavens.
The Lore of Life.
The Lore of Light.
The Lore of Beasts.
Learning magic with no master and no order of learned experts behind you is no easy task. How will you proceed?
You have chosen to study alone rather than under a Magister of [GetCollegeCharacterIsPartOf]. The college still opens its library and laboratories to you. How will you proceed?
I need more books and materials.
To the college library.
I'll experiment and see what happens.
I am ready to test myself.
The bigger your little laboratory grows, the better your chances of unlocking whatever power sleeps in you. But you still have a long way to go.
Night after night in the college library, by the light of a borrowed candle, you copy out treatises older than the Empire. You are learning, but you still have a long way to go.
Hmm...
You do not know exactly what you are doing, but you hope that patient trial and error will reveal the mysteries of the Winds of Magic.
In the laboratories of [GetCollegeCharacterIsPartOf] you try out the riskier spells you have read about, with sand buckets close at hand.
Now, if I mix this with that...
The explosion was mostly contained, but it still managed to wound you.
Damnation!
A flask bursts right in your face, and the potion slowly eats the skin off it.
Aaaarrgghh!!
This will be your last experiment. The blast has destroyed your laboratory and taken half your body with it.
Grrlllcht...
It has been hard to work it all out with no school and no master, but you have done it: you can feel your power and call on it with the proper words and gestures. You are a mage at last.
You tried your best, but without a master you are running blind. You will never learn magic this way.
Yes!
Damn.
Learning magic with no master and no order of learned experts behind you is hard enough. Necromancy is worse: every witch hunter in the Old World would burn you for trying. How will you proceed?
I need more books and materials.
I'll experiment and see what happens.
I am ready to test myself.
Forbidden texts are expensive and their sellers nervous, but your collection grows. Every page brings you closer to the secret of unlife, and you still have a long way to go.
Hmm...
You do not know exactly what you are doing, but you hope that patient trial and error will reveal the mysteries of death and unlife.
If only there were an easier way to find fresh corpses...

It is said the secret of necromancy lies in the clutches of the undead. Yet with the right resources you might find a copy of one of Nagash's books and reach enlightenment without grovelling at the feet of a vampire.
I shall search for the book.
This is beneath me. My will already moves the dead.
I will ask my dread liege for help.
I can manage on my own.

It has cost a small fortune and many months, but a copy of the Liber Mortis, written by the Great Necromancer himself, is in your hands. Now that you see the ancient book, you are not sure you can bear the secrets in its pages.
It's too late to turn back now!
I do not dare open it...
The secrets in the works of Nagash would break weaker minds, but not your will or your thirst for knowledge. You have found more in those old pages than you could have imagined.
Hmm...
The secrets in the works of Nagash would break weaker minds, but not your will or your thirst for knowledge.
Hmm...
You have learned much from the works of Nagash, but the cursed words have wormed their way into your mind, bringing twisted visions of the future and horrid hallucinations.
No! Get it away!

The secrets of the book were too much for you. The dark power bound in the writings of the Great Necromancer tore through your mind and left a withered husk. Perhaps someone luckier will carry on your work.
Hhhh...

You are an ancient King of Nehekhara, and the power of the dead is already part of your very essence. Thousands of servants rise at your command, answering their old master. Yet you cannot make more. Perhaps experimenting on your undead subjects might unlock the secret.
It is necessary.
I shall not harm my loyal servants.

Your servants have submitted to every experiment. In the orderly, repetitive fashion that is the hallmark of Nehekhara, you have made slow progress, and you begin to see the merit in Nagash's methods.
Good. Another hundred here.
Countless servants spent, countless days of study, and the secret of Nagash's necromancy still eludes you.
Curses.
Your vassal [From.GetFirstName] has taken an interest in necromancy. Clueless as [From.GetSheHe] is in matters of death and unlife, [From.GetSheHe] has wisely come to you for guidance.
Of course I will teach you.
I will teach you, but only if you abandon your gods.
Let me kiss you, and you shall know everything.
You are not worthy.
[From.GetFirstName] will help you uncover the secrets of the dark arts, but only if you forsake your gods and bow to the unliving.
As you command.
Never!
[From.GetFirstName] has accepted your terms and abandoned [From.GetHerHis] failed gods to follow you.
Good... Let me educate you.
[From.GetFirstName] has refused your terms, clinging to [From.GetHerHis] failed gods rather than learn the secrets of eternal life.
So be it.
[From.GetFirstName] has considered your request and agreed to help you, asking nothing in return.
A great gift. Thank you.

[From.GetFirstName] will help you, but only if you first let [From.GetHerHim] give you the Blood Kiss. Your studies, [From.GetSheHe] assures you, will be far easier once you are an immortal like [From.GetHerHim].
A great opportunity!
I wish to command the dead, not be one!
[From.GetFirstName] has accepted your offer and come to your chambers at night, bared [From.GetHerHis] throat, and received the Blood Kiss.
[From.GetFirstName] has stubbornly refused your gift, still too attached to [From.GetHerHis] fleeting life to see the wisdom of your offer.
So be it.
[From.GetFirstName] does not consider you worthy of [From.GetHerHis] ancient knowledge.
On my own, then. As usual.
It has been hard to work it all out with no school and no master, but you have done it. You are a necromancer. At your word, the dead walk and speak once more.
You tried your best, but without a guide you are running blind. You will never learn the secrets of undeath this way.
Rise!
Damnation.

[FromFrom.GetFirstName] has come to you in private, offering [FromFrom.GetHerHis] knowledge of the dark arts. For some reason [FromFrom.GetSheHe] believes you could become a powerful necromancer under [FromFrom.GetHerHis] guidance, if you take [FromFrom.GetHerHis] faith as your own.
It sounds intriguing...
Not interested.
[From.GetFirstName] has rejected your offer of power over death.
The fool.

Teaching necromancy is no easy task. Spirits slip their chains, corpses forget their purpose, and a careless pupil can raise more than [From.GetSheHe] can hold. What should [From.GetFirstName] focus on?
Caution is what matters most.
A necromancer needs daring.
Focus above everything.
It is time to test [From.GetHerHim].

[From.GetFirstName] spends long hours teaching you why a necromancer must be cautious. Never be surprised by how easily a spirit breaks its chains, or how quickly a horde of the dead loses its purpose.
I'll try to be careful.
[From.GetFirstName] spends long hours teaching you why a necromancer must be bold. Harden yourself to the horrors you will witness, and never hesitate.
I will.
[From.GetFirstName] spends long hours teaching you that a necromancer must stay calm and disciplined at all times, for the dead obey only an unwavering will.
Of course.
You have done it. Dark power flows through your veins, and the dead listen to your commands. You are a necromancer.
Despite your best efforts, necromancy is not for you. Your long years of study have qualified you for nothing but grave robbing.
Excellent.
Damnation.
[From.GetFirstName] has exceeded your expectations. At [From.GetHerHis] will, the dead walk again. Your work is done.
Good.
It seems your child [From.GetFirstName] has taken a dark path and mastered the art of necromancy.
I see...
[From.GetFirstName] has proved a failure. Despite your efforts, [From.GetSheHe] cannot master the dark arts.
What a waste.
It seems your child [From.GetFirstName] tried to master the art of necromancy and failed.
I see...
A sorcerer from the far steppes has come to your lands, claiming to have seen your future victories in visions sent by the Gods. The wanderer would settle at your court for a meagre price.
You are welcome here.
We have no such money to spare.
A shaman has come to your lands and won some favour among the locals. The soothsayer would join your court and read the bones for you, for a meagre price.
You are welcome here.
We have no such money to spare.

A mysterious visitor from the deserts has come to your court. He is, apparently, a famous scholar from a faraway land, versed in the arts of magic and the movements of the stars, and would stay and serve you for a meagre fee.
You are welcome here.
We have no such money to spare.

A travelling witch has decided to settle at your court. She has asked for a few things for her stay: a warm room, a cut of every hunt, and that nobody looks her in the eye. Refusing her would be... unwise.
You... are welcome here.
Send her back into the snow.
Witch's Curse
Turned a travelling witch away from the door, and she muttered something on her way out.

Since you were a child, strange things have happened around you. Candles gutter when you are angry. Dogs whine at you for no reason. Lately it has grown stronger: a pressure behind the eyes, a taste of iron on the air, colours at the edge of sight that nobody else seems to see. You know what it is. Everyone knows what it is. The question is who else will find out.
I have the gift! Why hide it?
Nobody must know. Nobody.
As time passes you still feel the twinge of magic. It is faint and far away, and you might not even recognise it if your people did not know so much about such things, but it is there.

As time passes you still feel the twinge of magic. Sometimes you seem to understand the meaning in an animal's cry, or move a cup without touching it. With a teacher, perhaps, it could become something.
There is no doubt any more: you are a wizard in the making. You have felt the Winds of Magic since childhood and instinctively tried to bend their flow. If only you found a teacher...

Even with your eyes closed you can see the Winds of Magic flowing through the world. Your gift is so strong that you have already warped reality by will alone, more than once, and not always on purpose.
I must know more!
[From.GetFirstName] has shown some crude talent for the arcane.
[From.GetFirstName] has shown a real talent for the arcane and, taught well, could become a capable wizard one day.
[From.GetFirstName] has a clear gift for magic. With a teacher [From.GetSheHe] could become a truly powerful wizard.
Seldom has anyone seen such a natural as [From.GetFirstName]. With proper training [From.GetSheHe] could become one of the greatest wizards of the age. Or one of the most dangerous.
Something to ponder...
My court mage will take [From.GetHerHim] as an apprentice.
Luckily the strange feeling is only a faint twitch at the edge of your mind. You have buried it and walled it off. Magic is bad news, and you will keep this to yourself.
The strange feeling is only a twitch at the edge of your mind, and you have buried it deep. When magic is concerned it is better to say nothing, even when you are the one who rules.

You have felt the Winds of Magic since childhood and instinctively tried to bend them. It has always frightened you, almost as much as what your vassals and your priests would do if they knew. You will keep it hidden.

Even with your eyes closed you can see the Winds of Magic. You have already warped reality by will alone more than once, and it takes all your strength not to do it again. You fear what would happen if your secret came out.
Why me?
I don't care! I won't hide who I am.
Luckily the strange feeling is only a faint twitch at the edge of your mind. You have buried it and walled it off. It must stay hidden from the court and, above all, from your lord.
The strange feeling is only a twitch at the edge of your mind, and you have buried it deep. When magic is concerned it is better to say nothing to the court and, above all, to your lord.

You have felt the Winds of Magic since childhood and instinctively tried to bend them. It has always frightened you, almost as much as what your lord would do if [Root.Liege.GetSheHe] knew. You will keep it hidden from everyone.

Even with your eyes closed you can see the Winds of Magic. You have already warped reality by will alone more than once, and it takes all your strength not to do it again. You fear what your lord would do if your secret came out.
Why me?
You had barely understood the gift yourself, but your lord has keener eyes. A careless word, a flicker at the wrong moment, and [Root.Liege.GetFirstName] knows.
Since childhood you have feared that your gift would betray you one day. Today is that day: [Root.Liege.GetFirstName] has found out.
Wait! I can explain!
It was hard to spot, but you are certain now: [From.GetFirstName] has some connection to the Winds of Magic, and has hidden it from you.
How could it go unnoticed for so long? [From.GetFirstName] has a strong connection to the Winds of Magic, and has hidden it from you.
How could it go unnoticed for so long? [From.GetFirstName] has a terrifying connection to the Winds of Magic. Left unchecked, who knows what [From.GetSheHe] might become.
Burn [From.GetHerHim]!
A [From.GetBoyGirl] with the gift? It must not be. Hollow [From.GetHerHim].
He might be the one the prophecy warns of! Kill him!
This is no concern of mine.
Witch! Witch! Witch!

You have been found out at last. The witch hunters learned of your dark arts and forbidden knowledge, and with your lord's blessing they broke down your door at dawn. Now the firewood is stacked high in the square, and the crowd is already chanting.
I curse you ALL!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been burned at the stake for witchcraft.
Don't trouble me with these things again.
I see...

[witch_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] of the Ice Witches has come for you. She has followed the cold trail of your spells to your door: a man reaching for the winds, which Kislevite law forbids and which, the Sisterhood says, brings the old prophecy closer. She means to see you judged.

[witch_hunter.GetTitledFirstName], a Damsel of the Lady, has come for you. She has followed the trail of your spells to your door: a man reaching for the winds, which the Lady forbids to men. She means to see you judged.
I appeal to my lord!
Throw this witch out of my lands.
Throw this witch in my dungeon.

[witch_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] of the Ice Witches has exposed [From.GetTitledFirstName] as an unsanctioned wizard. Whatever his intentions, by opening his mind to the Winds of Magic he risks fulfilling the prophecy and dooming all of Kislev. She demands that he be stopped.
[witch_hunter.GetTitledFirstName], a Damsel of the Lady, has exposed [From.GetTitledFirstName] as a man who wields magic. The Lady permits no such thing, and the Damsel demands that he be stopped.
Burn him!
Cut him off from the winds.
No. He is innocent.
The accused is burned at the stake.
The accused is hollowed: cut off from the Winds of Magic forever, and stripped of any lands.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has ruled against you. The witch's people seize you, and before the day is out you are bound to a stake in the square.
Nooooo!

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has ruled against you. The witch lays her cold hands on your head and tears something out of you that you never knew could be torn. The winds are gone. The world is grey and silent, and it always will be.
Nooooo!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has ruled in your favour. The witch leaves, but she looks back once at the door, and you know you have not been forgotten.
A close call!

Your studies have been disturbed of late by waves of unfamiliar magic. You have followed them to their source: a woman at court who studies the arts in secret. The Prophets teach that women fall more easily to the corruption of the dead, and so the law forbids it. It is your duty to expose her.
I'll confront her.
[From.GetTitledFirstName], a scholar of the court, has discovered your forbidden studies and come to confront you.
I appeal to my lord!
Throw this scholar out of my lands.
Throw this scholar in my dungeon.

[arabyan_scholar.GetTitledFirstName] has exposed [From.GetTitledFirstName] as a woman who studies magic. By reading forbidden texts and touching the holy fire she risks corrupting herself and your lands, and the scholar demands that she be stopped.
Burn her!
Cut her off from the winds.
No. She is innocent.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has ruled against you. The scholar's men take you before dawn, and the fire is already lit.
Nooooo!

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has ruled against you. The scholar binds you with words older than the city and cuts the winds out of you. Women were never meant to wield this knowledge, he says. Your insolence will cost you far more than magic.
Nooooo!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has ruled in your favour. The scholar will leave you alone, for now.
A close call!
The Magic Menace

A startling turn of events. Our [From.GetTitle] has determined that [From.GetReasonToRelaxMagicLaws]
The new law decrees [From.GetNewMagicRights]

The witch hunters are already muttering in the taverns, and the priests in their pulpits.

Our [From.GetTitle] has determined that [From.GetReasonToExpandMagicLaws]
The new law decrees [From.GetNewMagicRights]

The hedge wizards are packing their bags, and the witch hunters are sharpening their stakes.
This was a necessary step.
A good choice.
The end times are near!

[scoped_magic_ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has clearly lost [scoped_magic_ruler.GetHerHis] mind. Yet with the authority [scoped_magic_ruler.GetSheHe] has gathered, [scoped_magic_ruler.GetSheHe] might yet turn our realm into a nest of sorcerers and a door for the Dark Gods. [scoped_magic_ruler.GetSheHeCap] must be stopped now, before it is too late!

[scoped_magic_ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has clearly lost [scoped_magic_ruler.GetHerHis] mind, persecuting magic in our realm once more. With the authority [scoped_magic_ruler.GetSheHe] has gathered, [scoped_magic_ruler.GetSheHe] might turn our realm into a land of superstitious fools and burning pyres. [scoped_magic_ruler.GetSheHeCap] must be stopped now, before it is too late!
We must rise up and depose this tyrant!
Send letters urging every lord of the realm to band together against the madman on the throne.
There is nothing we can do.

To all the faithful!\nMadness has taken our [scoped_magic_ruler.GetTitle]. Sorcerers walk free at court, and the Dark Gods are laughing. We must stand together and depose the fool on the throne, or watch Chaos spread across our land.\n[From.GetTitledName]

To my fellow lords! Do not believe the lies of the superstitious!\nMadness has taken our [scoped_magic_ruler.GetTitle]. We must stand together and depose the fool on the throne, or see our families and our people burned at the stake on the whims of witch hunters!\n[From.GetTitledName]
Death to the tyrant!
These are the words of a traitor.
The time has come!\nAll of us who suffer under the yoke of our mad [scoped_magic_ruler.GetTitle] have gathered under my banner, and we are ready to bring the tyrant to justice.
To war!

Several indignant vassals have banded together against the new magic law. They have taken up arms to overthrow their own [scoped_magic_ruler.GetTitle] and restore what they call the rightful way of things.
Traitors, all of them!
I cannot say I am surprised...
A New Day

One of your commanders is a mage or a daemon summoner, and is besieging an enemy holding.\n\nFrom the second month of a siege, each such commander wears down the defences.
